svg.text: AUCTION — BID FLOW & PROXY WAR
THE RACE — two bidders, one price
Auction A-9 is ACTIVE, currentPrice = 100, increment = 10
T1 → placeBid(A-9, Ana, 110)
T2 → placeBid(A-9, Bo, 115)
T3 → placeBid(A-9, seller, 200)
unguarded, both T1 and T2 could read price=100
and each declare itself the winner
T3 is shill bidding — rejected before any lock
is taken (IllegalStateException, not a false return)
seller guard — throws
synchronized Auction.placeBid
one monitor per Auction → T1 and T2 serialise here
delegates to state.placeBid(this, bid) — STATE
ActiveAuctionState: now > endTime → false
amount ≤ currentPrice → false
else recordAcceptedBid(bid)
bids.add · currentPrice = amount · winningBidderId = bidder
all three fields move together ⇒ the auction never lies ✓
true
false
ACCEPTED
bid.accept() · price and winner updated
that bidder's older bids are superseded
then → proxy resolution pass
REJECTED
bid.reject(); placeBid returns false
no exception — losing is a normal outcome
also the answer for SCHEDULED / COMPLETED / CANCELLED
THE EXPIRY SWEEPER
single daemon thread "auction-expiry"
scheduleAtFixedRate(expireAuctions, 1s, 1s)
for each auction: ACTIVE && now > endTime → end()
honest: a 1-second poll, so an auction can sit
"ACTIVE" for up to a second past its end time
but placeBid re-checks the clock itself, so no
late bid is ever accepted — the poll is cosmetic ✓
daemon ⇒ JVM exits cleanly; shutdown() stops it explicitly
THE PROXY WAR — every accepted bid triggers a counter-bid pass
Ana registered a proxy with max 500. Bo registered max 300. Cy bids 100 by hand. increment = 10.
time
Cy bids 100 manually → accepted, currentPrice = 100
resolve: skip Cy · candidates {Ana 500, Bo 300} → best = Ana
counter at min(nextMinimumBid = 110, 500) = 110 → accepted
resolve again: skip Ana · Bo 300 > 110 → Bo counters 120
… Ana 130, Bo 140, Ana 150 … ratcheting by the increment
at 300 Bo's max is exhausted — no proxy beats currentPrice
Ana wins at ~310 — NOT at her 500 cap
Termination is provable:
every accepted bid strictly raises currentPrice,
and every proxy has a finite max → the recursion
must run out of eligible proxies.
Only ONE proxy counters per pass — the highest max.
That is what produces second-price behaviour: the
winner pays just enough to beat the runner-up.
Honest: the pass runs OUTSIDE the auction monitor.
It reads currentPrice, picks a proxy, then calls placeBid.
A manual bid landing in that gap makes the counter stale —
it is then simply rejected, and the next pass re-counters.
Safe, but it can burn a wasted round. Fix: resolve inside the monitor.
AUCTION LIFECYCLE — only ACTIVE takes bids
create
SCHEDULED
placeBid → false
start()
ACTIVE
the only bidding state
end()
or the 1s sweeper
COMPLETED
winningBidderId is the winner
cancel()
CANCELLED
no winner, bids stay on record
COMPLETED and CANCELLED are terminal:
start / end / cancel are no-ops
placeBid returns false
no winner is "computed" at the end — the winner
is whoever held winningBidderId when time ran out ✓
honest: no reserve price, and the winner's Bid is never
flipped to WINNING at end() — win() exists but is unused
payment/settlement is entirely out of scope here
WHITEBOARD ORDER:

① two bidders racing one price (+ the seller guard) → ② synchronized Auction.placeBid delegating to the state → ③ the 1s expiry sweeper → ④ the proxy counter-bid ratchet → ⑤ SCHEDULED → ACTIVE → COMPLETED / CANCELLED
THE FOUR INVARIANTS

g.text: ② price, winner and bid list mutate under one monitor.
③ A seller can never bid on their own item.

svg.text: LEGEND

g.text: Per-auction monitor · proxy counter-bid ratchet · 1s daemon expiry sweep — LLD
